subject: Edenbridge post-demo model trio + ops risk log

Date: 2027-07-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Edenbridge post-demo model trio + ops risk log

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the recommended model trio for the POC based on the demo prompts and latency targets you shared (90th pct <= 350ms for single-turn FAQ/assist flows):

1) Compact low-latency (recommended for latency-sensitive widgets)
   - Model: redwood-small-quant (8-bit)
   - Rationale: sub-200ms median, lowest cost; reasonable for short-turn Q/A and autofill where hallucination risk is low.
   - Estimated unit cost: ~$0.6 / 1k tokens (in our hosted pricing mix)

2) Balanced mid-tier (default POC recommendation)
   - Model: redwood-medium-slate
   - Rationale: best tradeoff of quality vs latency for mixed prompts (multi-sentence context, follow-up queries). Hits your accuracy bar on our demo prompt set while staying <350ms 90th with batching.
   - Estimated unit cost: ~$1.8 / 1k tokens

3) High-quality contextual (for long-form synthesis and high-risk responses)
   - Model: redwood-large-ft (quant-friendly)
   - Rationale: top-quality responses with improved context retention and fewer regressions on hallucination-sensitive prompts. Expect higher cost and higher 90th latency (~500ms) — plan to use as fallback for critical flows.
   - Estimated unit cost: ~$3.6 / 1k tokens

Benchmark links and artifacts attached:
- Benchmarks (latency, token-cost breakdown, prompt-level regression flags): https://drive.redwood.ai/edenbridge/benchmarks_q2
- Prompt pack we used (anonymized): edenbridge_prompt_set_v1.json (attached)
- Sample cost model (spreadsheet): benchmarks_edenbridge_q2.xlsx (attached)

Operational notes / regression concerns:
- Prompt drift: medium-tier showed occasional quality drift on multi-step legal-extraction prompts; we flagged 6 prompts with regression risk.
- Tokenization differences: Compact quantized path truncates longer contexts — we recommend prefix-preserving cache for widgets.
- Fallback policy: We suggest routing to high-quality model only for predicted-high-risk queries (confidence threshold) to control spend.

Recommended next steps (suggested timeline):
- Week 0: Hand-off artifacts and prompt set (done)
- Week 1: Sandbox benchmarks + 2-day smoke run on your representative traffic (we can run hosted or spin dedicated pool)
- Week 2: Canary rollout (5% of production traffic) with telemetry hooks and regression tests

Can you confirm preferred environment (hosted vs. dedicated) and whether procurement should be looped now? I'll also attach a short mutual action plan template if helpful.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the benchmark spreadsheet line-by-line.

— Avery

- Procurement: please loop procurement@edenbridge.ai; they want an initial estimate to include in the RFP packet.

Also, small ask: can you produce a short mutual action plan (1 page) that lists owners and milestones? That will speed internal approvals.

Hi Sam — looping in a few concrete artifacts to move quickly.

1) Hosted vs Dedicated cost delta (high level):
   - Hosted: lower up-front friction; our estimates from the attached spreadsheet show ~15–18% higher per-token unit cost for sustained traffic due to pooled infra. Good if you want fast start.
   - Dedicated: commit-based discounts; with a 12-month reserved capacity we can reduce unit cost for the mid-tier model by ~28% vs hosted (numbers in worksheet).

2) The 6 flagged prompts (excerpted):
   - Prompt IDs: P-1042, P-1047, P-1053, P-1091, P-1100, P-1107 — each has short notes in the attached prompt pack (edenbridge_prompt_set_v1.json) under "regression_notes". We anonymized customer content per your request.

3) Mutual action plan (short):
   - Owner: Edenbridge Product (Sam) — review flagged prompts (due 2027-07-25)
   - Owner: Redwood SE (Avery) — run sandbox benchmarks and share per-prompt logs (due 2027-07-27)
   - Owner: Edenbridge Eng (procurement cc) — decision on hosted vs dedicated (due 2027-08-03)
   - Owner: Redwood Ops (Ben) — prepare canary config + SLA proposal (due 2027-08-10)

4) Rollout guardrails:
   - Canary at 5% + automated quality checks against the prompt pack (fail if regression rate > 4% on critical prompts)
   - Auto-fallback to mid-tier model on spikes > 2x baseline latency

HubSpot link for the deal and internal trackers: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-9082

I'll attach a 1-page MAP (mutual action plan) to an upcoming email. Thursday 10am PST works for the demo deep-dive — I'll send a calendar invite.

— Ben
